# 4 Maccabees Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Eleazar's Martyrdom

---

**1** Eleazar was brought before the tribunal and bound by the soldiers. They ordered him once more to eat the forbidden meat.

**2** But Eleazar — a man of true dignity and integrity — did not shrink from what he had to say:

**3** Antiochus, we are not going to be forced so easily into eating defiled food. The law is our teacher, and we know it speaks truth.

**4** The guards seized him, brought him to the torture devices, and tore open his sides with hooks, trying to force meat into his mouth through his wounds.

**5** But Eleazar did not crack. Even as he was being tortured, he raised his eyes toward heaven and said:

**6** God, you know I could have saved myself. But I am dying in these flames for the sake of your law.

**7** Have mercy on your people. Let my suffering be enough for them.

**8** Accept my blood as their purification. Receive my life as a ransom for theirs.

**9** With those words, the holy man died with honor — enduring the torments by the power of reason grounded in devotion.

**10** Eleazar was the first to walk the path of holy martyrdom.

**11** In him we see reason at work — a priest not losing himself even in the grip of fire and pain.

**12** He bore his suffering not because he had to but because he chose to — for the sake of the law.

**13** What a sacred battle! What a noble wrestler of the divine law! What a victory of devotion over bodily passion!

**14** Eleazar, priest and philosopher, you were not broken by the tyrant's cruelty or burned into surrender by the flames.

**15** You were an athlete of the divine commandments, clothed in the armor of devotion — an armor that fire cannot destroy — and through it you defeated the enemy.

**16** In you, father of our nation, the law showed its power — for through holy reason, you proved that reason is master of the passions.

**17** Eleazar, you did not defile your sacred lips with forbidden food even to buy yourself another moment of life, and you did not shame your old age for the sake of a bodily appetite.

**18** You kept the beauty of your holy old age intact through the nobility of your choices.

**19** In you, the mastery of reason over the passions was made plain for all to see.

**20** Holy and honored is the death of those who die for the law.

**21** Blessed are you, Eleazar! You have been given the imperishable prizes of eternal life.

**22** You lit a flame of devotion for all of Israel that day, and your self-discipline showed what it means to put reason above pleasure.

**23** At ninety years old you were not weakened by bodily desires but remained vigorous through reason.

**24** While the fire burned around him and torturers wielded their instruments, he held his gaze steady upward, his soul undefeated.

**25** O priest clothed in the philosophy of the law! O elder devoted to its holiness! O life faithful to the ancient ways!

**26** By his nobility, Eleazar became the pioneer of all who die for their faith.

**27** Without question, this man's devotion sanctified the suffering of the whole nation and broke the back of the tyranny over it.

**28** For what Eleazar endured was sufficient to make the nation holy.

**29** The king himself was held back from advancing further against the holy city by what this death had demonstrated.

**30** Through the nobility of his death, Eleazar became the beginning of purification for all Israel.
